title: lock has no --created; wall-clock timestamp is inside lock_hash, breaking reproducibility
description:
VERIFIED on lock 0.6.0 / pack 0.6.0 (2026-09-02) against 123 real SEC ABS-EE filings.

Two runs of the SAME pipeline over BYTE-IDENTICAL inputs produce different lockfiles:
  run1 lock_hash=sha256:34c2115a...  created=2026-09-02T14:41:07Z
  run2 lock_hash=sha256:9c252028...  created=2026-09-02T14:41:44Z
Member content is identical (123/123 verify in both). Only 'created' differs, and it is inside lock_hash.

DOWNSTREAM EFFECT: this is the only non-deterministic link in the whole seal chain. Sealing the SAME lockfile twice yields an identical pack_id, so pack is reproducible. Sealing a pipeline that regenerates the lock does not:
  same lockfile   -> pack_id sha256:dbfa7595...  (identical both runs)
  regenerated lock-> pack_id sha256:3e04b101... vs sha256:85670934...
So 'same inputs produce the same sealed evidence pack' is false today purely because of this field.

INCONSISTENT WITH ITS SIBLING: pack seal already exposes
  --created <RFC3339>  Reproducible manifest creation timestamp (RFC3339, normalized to UTC)
lock has --as-of (semantic point-in-time), --dataset-id and --note, but no --created. Same tool family, same problem, one solved and one not.

ALSO INCONSISTENT WITH THE STATED DOCTRINE: byte-deterministic domain artifacts are supposed to stay free of volatile telemetry, with timestamps living in receipts and the run ledger. A lockfile is a domain artifact - it IS the pinned dataset identity - and it carries wall-clock provenance inside its hash.

FIX, either:
  1. Add --created <RFC3339> to lock, mirroring pack seal exactly. Smallest change, restores parity, keeps 'created' auditable. Recommended.
  2. Move 'created' outside lock_hash so it is provenance metadata rather than identity. Cleaner semantically but changes the hash for every existing lockfile.

Option 1 preferred - it matches a contract that already exists in the same family.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated runs with identical JSONL and the same explicit creation timestamp emit byte-identical lock JSON and lock_hash.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-10-27 (validated, root-caused)
Problem: Identical JSONL inputs produce different lock hashes across runs because `created` is generated from wall-clock time, included in the self-hash, and has no caller-controlled value.
Root cause: `src/cli/mod.rs:21-35` has no created override. `src/lib.rs:151,160,178-179` sets created from Utc::now() and then hashes the lockfile; `src/lockfile/self_hash.rs:14-20` serializes it before SHA256.
Validated: No bead dependencies. Confirmed in the local tree and live GitHub default branch: no --created option; each run stamps Utc::now() before hashing. Did not replay the 123 SEC filings or pack-id measurements.
Evidence: src/cli/mod.rs:21-35; GitHub default branch cmdrvl/lock/src/cli/mod.rs: no created option; src/lib.rs:151,160,178-179; GitHub default branch cmdrvl/lock/src/lib.rs: Utc::now() timestamp precedes hash computation; src/lockfile/self_hash.rs:14-20: serializes the complete Lockfile and hashes canonical JSON; docs/PLAN.md:502,853: same created timestamp is required for deterministic output; GitHub default branch cmdrvl/pack/src/cli/args.rs exposes --created
Done when: Repeated runs with identical JSONL and the same explicit creation timestamp emit byte-identical lock JSON and lock_hash.

title: Add description to --root in 'lock verify --help'
description:
## Problem

\`lock verify --help\` shows:

```
Options:
      --root <DIR>
```

No description. The flag means "resolve member paths relative to this directory for content hash verification" but you have to guess or read --describe JSON to learn this.

## Observed behavior (spring11 session)

After creating the lockfile, we ran:

```bash
lock verify normalized/sales-comp-grids.lock.json
# → VERIFY_OK (self-hash only)
```

Then wondered: "did it actually check the file contents?" Had to discover --root by reading --describe JSON, then guessed the semantics:

```bash
lock verify normalized/sales-comp-grids.lock.json --root normalized/
# → VERIFY_OK, 3/3 members verified
```

The word "root" is ambiguous — root of the project? filesystem root? The --describe JSON has a good explanation ("Root directory for member verification. Without this, only self-hash is checked.") but --help shows nothing.

## Expected

```
Options:
      --root <DIR>   Root directory for resolving member paths (enables content verification)
```

## Notes

- lock 0.2.0
- The --describe operator.v0 JSON has excellent documentation for this — it just needs to surface in --help

title: Add --output flag to avoid self-inclusion when lockfile lands inside vacuum root
description:
## Problem

lock writes to stdout. The canonical pipeline is:

```bash
vacuum normalized/ | hashbytes | lock --dataset-id X > normalized/lock.json
```

But this creates a race: the shell creates \`normalized/lock.json\` (0 bytes) before vacuum scans the directory. vacuum picks up the empty lockfile, hashbytes hashes it as 0 bytes, and lock pins it. After lock finishes writing, the file is ~1KB. On verify:

```
VERIFY_FAILED
  normalized/lock.json: SIZE_MISMATCH (expected 0, got 1002)
```

The lockfile hashed itself while empty, then grew.

## Workaround used (spring11 session)

Write to /tmp first, then copy in:

```bash
vacuum normalized/ | hashbytes | lock --dataset-id X > /tmp/lock.json
command cp /tmp/lock.json normalized/sales-comp-grids.lock.json
lock verify normalized/sales-comp-grids.lock.json --root normalized/
# → VERIFY_OK
```

This works but is fragile and non-obvious. Every user will hit this the first time.

## Suggested fix

Add \`--output <path>\` that:
1. Writes the lockfile to the specified path
2. Automatically excludes that path from the member list (or writes after manifest is sealed)

Alternatively, document the /tmp pattern prominently in --help.

## Notes

- lock 0.2.0
- Also hit macOS shell alias friction: \`rm\` aliased to \`rm -i\` blocked the cleanup; had to use \`command rm -f\`
- This is the single biggest sharp edge in the entire spine pipeline
acceptance_criteria: 1. lock --output <path> writes lockfile to specified path instead of stdout. 2. The output path is automatically excluded from the member list (or written after manifest is sealed). 3. Pipe-based workflow (vacuum | hashbytes | lock --output out.lock) produces a self-consistent lockfile. 4. lock verify out.lock --root <dir> returns VERIFY_OK without the /tmp workaround. 5. --describe documents the --output flag. 6. --help shows --output with description.

title: Witness since/until filtering uses lexicographic timestamp comparison
description:
lock witness query/count currently compare RFC3339 timestamps as raw strings in matches_filters (src/witness/mod.rs), which can produce incorrect results when records or filter values use non-Z offsets.

2. Run: lock witness query --since 2025-12-31T22:45:00Z --json.
3. Expected: +02:00 record excluded based on absolute time; actual behavior may differ due to string compare.

Impact:
- User-facing correctness bug in witness query/count filtering.
- Misleading counts/results for mixed-offset ledgers, affecting audits/debugging.

Proposed fix scope:
- Parse filter and record timestamps with chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339 and compare normalized instants.
- Define fallback behavior for unparsable timestamps and cover with tests.
- Add mixed-offset and malformed-timestamp test cases.

title: Prevent symlink escapes outside --root and enforce regular-file check in lock verify
description:
## Evidence (Source Audit)
- `src/verify/members.rs:70-96` resolves `root.join(member_path)` and calls `fs::metadata(&full_path)` (which follows symlinks) without verifying canonical containment inside `--root` or checking `metadata.is_file()`.
- Also `verify_members` is `pub` and performs no path safety check itself if invoked directly outside CLI validation.

## Impact
A symlink inside `--root` pointing to a sensitive file outside `--root` (e.g., `/etc/passwd` or a protected file) is followed, hashed, and its size/hash reported by `lock verify`.

## Fix
1. Guard `verify_members` defensively against absolute / `..` paths.
2. Canonicalize `root` and each resolved member path (or inspect `symlink_metadata`), failing verification deterministically if the target escapes `root` or is not a regular file.
acceptance_criteria:
- Symlink inside `--root` pointing outside `--root` fails `lock verify` deterministically without hashing the external target.
- Non-regular files (directories/FIFOs) fail cleanly.
- Regression tests cover out-of-root symlinks and direct `verify_members` calls with traversal paths.

title: Implement Level 2 member filesystem verification
description:
Create src/verify/members.rs. For each member in the lockfile: resolve path against --root, check existence (MISSING), stat size (SIZE_MISMATCH), stream-read and hash using algorithm prefix from stored bytes_hash (sha256 via sha2 crate, blake3 via blake3 crate). IO errors become skips (IO_ERROR) not failures. Build MembersResult with checked/verified/failed/skipped counts and failure/skip detail arrays. Outcome logic: all verified=VERIFY_OK, any failed=VERIFY_FAILED, no failed + some skipped=VERIFY_PARTIAL (or VERIFY_FAILED if --strict).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each member resolved as <root>/<member.path>
- Missing file → MemberFailure with reason MISSING, actual fields null
- Size mismatch → MemberFailure with reason SIZE_MISMATCH (hash skipped)
- Hash mismatch → MemberFailure with reason HASH_MISMATCH, actual hash included
- IO error during read → MemberSkip with reason IO_ERROR and OS error detail
- sha256: prefix → uses SHA256; blake3: prefix → uses BLAKE3
- Streaming hash (not loading full file into memory)
- MembersResult counts are consistent: checked = verified + failed + skipped
- --strict promotes VERIFY_PARTIAL (skips but no failures) to VERIFY_FAILED
- All members pass → VERIFY_OK
- Module-level unit tests: each failure reason, each skip reason, count consistency, strict promotion
